question: Should OpenClaw core define and own a cross-gateway session messaging contract now, or keep this behind plugin/bridge APIs until a broader federation design is accepted?
rationale: The requested behavior crosses gateway trust boundaries and session ownership, so the implementation shape is a maintainer product/security decision rather than a narrow bug fix.

options.title: Design core contract first
options.body: Define identity, authorization, delivery, replay, and session-history semantics before landing a core session-tool implementation.

options.title: Bridge or plugin first
options.body: Keep core gateway-local and expose only missing plugin or MCP bridge seams if external implementations need them.

options.title: Defer to federation FRD
options.body: Hold this concrete feature until broader gateway federation work such as https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/87733 decides the transport and trust model.

recommendation.title: Design core contract first
recommendation.body: Define identity, authorization, delivery, replay, and session-history semantics before landing a core session-tool implementation.

likelyOwner.reason: The strongest history trail for session-tool architecture, gatewayUrl security, and session resolution points to this owner candidate.
